description: Detected SQL injection vulnerability: unsanitized user input concatenated directly into SQL query string. Parameterized queries must be used instead.
remediation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries (e.g., using `db.Query` with `?` placeholders in Go). Validate and sanitize all user inputs.

description: Hardcoded database password detected in source code. Credentials must never be stored in plaintext in the codebase.
remediation: Move the database password to environment variables or a secure vault (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager). Remove all hardcoded credentials from source files.

description: Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability: user-supplied data is rendered in HTML without proper escaping or sanitization.
remediation: Use context-aware output encoding (HTML entity encoding). Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers. Use a templating engine with auto-escaping enabled.

description: Command injection vulnerability: user-controlled input is passed to `exec.Command` without validation. An attacker could execute arbitrary system commands.
remediation: Avoid shell execution entirely. Use safer alternatives like `os/exec` with fixed arguments. Validate and sanitize any input passed to system commands.

description: Use of weak cryptographic algorithm (MD5) for password hashing. MD5 is considered broken and vulnerable to collision attacks.
remediation: Replace MD5 with bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 for password hashing. For general hashing use SHA-256 or SHA-3.

description: Critical vulnerability in dependency `lodash` v4.17.20 (CVE-2021-23337) allowing prototype pollution and potential remote code execution.
remediation: Update `lodash` to version 4.17.21 or later. Run `npm update lodash` and verify no breaking changes. Review dependency tree for other vulnerable transitive dependencies.
